aspect: EXAMPLE - fuzzy matching against a sanctions list
description: Screening systems match approximately. A common Persian name can collide with a listed individual, dropping an ordinary transaction into manual review where the customer must prove they are not someone else.
energy_note: Proving a negative about a stranger who shares your name.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the Apple Store heard the language, not the name
description: In 2012 an Apple employee refused a sale after overhearing Farsi. The trigger does not even need to be written down - speaking is enough (see DIS-003).

Many people apply under a shortened or Anglicised first name. Where the callback rate improves, that improvement is itself the evidence - and the cost is borne silently by the person who edited their own name to get an interview.
money_note: Foregone earnings where it does not work - illustrative.
energy_note: Editing your name to be employable.

description: Being addressed by the wrong name for an hour, or watching an interviewer decide not to attempt it, is a small thing that happens in every professional interaction for a lifetime.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the email address gives it away
description: Even where a CV is anonymised, the email address, the university and the country of the phone number restore the signal.

aspect: SCENARIO - the CV that got callbacks
description: After eleven months and about ninety applications, Omid changes the name on his CV to 'Ohm Hoseini' and his email to a first-initial address. He gets three callbacks in five weeks. He does not tell anyone he did this, including his sister.
energy_note: The experiment works, and that is the worst part.
